newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve firms on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve firms on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards rose around 20 basis points across the board, with a forex-linked liquidity shortage boosting rates at the short end, dealers said.
"All rates are up 20 basis points and the shorts trade even higher," said a senior dealer at a private bank. "There is concern that forex outflows might continue today."
The trader said profit taking by investors with positions in ecu/drachma mainly accounted for Monday's outflows.

"Traders realise that we are approaching the end of the year and ecu/drachma is still low compared to 303 levels the same period in 1995," he said. "They also know that the central bank wants ecu/drachma higher and they gradually square positions taking their nice profit."
The dealer added that only a small part of Monday's outflows was due to FRN selling by players worried about a retroactive tax on outstanding FRNs.
Other traders said there was a tighter link between tax talk and ecu buying by commercial banks at Monday's fixing.
Forex outflows valued at a total of 250 million ecus took place at the fixing driving ecu/drachma over the 302 drachma level. Lighter buying of forex for drachmas continued after the fixing.

Traders said the thorny issue was whether the government would choose to tax outstanding FRNs. A high-level national economy ministry official told Reuters on Monday that the government was leaning against taxing outstanding FRNs.
The mark was quoted at 157.60/65 drachmas from Monday's 157.530 fix, the dollar at 238.07/17 drachmas from 238.210 and the Ecu at 302.36/46 from 302.120 drachmas.
